title: Mercury Has Gotten Smaller Than We Thought - Nautilus
gist: Mercury has shrunk more than previously thought. The visible text explains why Mercury is hard to reach: the sun's gravity well forced NASA's MESSENGER, launched in 2004, to spend until 2011 using Earth and Venus flybys before entering orbit.

insights.claim: Although Mercury is about 100 million miles closer to Earth than Mars, reaching it takes much longer: NASA's MESSENGER launched in 2004 but entered Mercury orbit only in 2011, while the 2005 Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter reached Mars in under a year.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Delta-v, not distance, drives mission cost and timelines, which matters for evaluating space mission economics.

insights.claim: The sun's massive gravity well rules out a direct trajectory to Mercury because a spacecraft would arrive too fast to decelerate, so MESSENGER used Earth and Venus gravity assists to spiral in.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Inner-solar-system missions need long gravity-assist campaigns, a structural constraint on timelines.

insights.claim: Mercury has contracted more than scientists previously estimated, with its surface 'hiding its wrinkles'.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Planetary science finding with no direct market angle; the details are cut off in the text.
